gloss: native Japanese words; words of Japanese origin

definitions.gloss: native Japanese words; words of Japanese origin
definitions.explanation: Words that originated in the Japanese language before the introduction of Chinese loanwords (漢語) and Western loanwords (外来語). Also called 和語. These words are typically read with kun'yomi when written in kanji.

examples.japanese: 「{花|はな}」は{大和言葉|やまとことば}だ。
{大和言葉|やまとことば}には{柔|やわ}らかい{響|ひび}きがある。
examples.english: Native Japanese words have a soft ring to them.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{語彙|ごい}は{大和言葉|やまとことば}、{漢語|かんご}、{外来語|がいらいご}の3つに{大|おお}きく{分|わ}けられる。
examples.english: Japanese vocabulary is broadly divided into three categories: native Japanese words, Sino-Japanese words, and foreign loanwords.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{大和言葉|やまとことば} (also written {和語|わご}) refers to the indigenous vocabulary of Japanese, as distinct from {漢語|かんご} (Sino-Japanese words borrowed from Chinese) and {外来語|がいらいご} (Western loanwords).

Examples of {大和言葉|やまとことば}:
- {山|やま} (mountain), {川|かわ} (river), {空|そら} (sky)
- {美|うつく}しい (beautiful), {嬉|うれ}しい (happy)
- {食|た}べる (to eat), {歩|ある}く (to walk)

{大和言葉|やまとことば} tends to convey softer, more emotional nuances compared to {漢語|かんご}, which often sounds more formal or technical. For instance, {思|おも}いやり ({大和言葉|やまとことば}) vs {配慮|はいりょ} ({漢語|かんご}) — both mean consideration/thoughtfulness, but the native word feels warmer.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大和言葉|やまとことば}の{美|うつく}しさ (the beauty of native Japanese words)
- {大和言葉|やまとことば}で{表現|ひょうげん}する (express in native Japanese words)
